us11304793b2_analysis.title: Methods, systems and devices for treatment of cerebrospinal venous insufficiency and multiple sclerosis
claim_1_elements: Method for treating rising venous backpressure affecting cerebrospinal vein
Self-expanding stent in RIGHT INTERNAL JUGULAR VEIN (IJV)
Sensor sensing physiological trigger (rising venous backpressure)
Microprocessor automatically actuating stent to different force
Deformable constraining member → variable expansion (first → second configuration)
Varying force in response to sensor → CLOSED-LOOP
what_is_covered: Adaptive sensing stent in cerebrospinal vein
what_is_NOT_specifically_claimed: Transverse sinus or sigmoid sinus (claim specifies IJV)
IIH / pseudotumor cerebri (claims are for MS / neurodegenerative)
CSF pressure regulation (focuses on venous backpressure, not CSF)
us11304793b2_analysis.section_102: NOT directly anticipated for transverse/sigmoid sinus + IIH (different anatomy, different disease)
us11304793b2_analysis.section_103: SERIOUS THREAT — combining adaptive cerebrospinal vein stent (US11304793B2) with VSS for IIH (known) is arguably obvious

ce_014_false_negative_search_lesson.lesson: No result for our formulation is not evidence that the capability is absent. Patent searches must generate terminology from patent claims + descriptions + CPC classes + inventor vocabulary + adjacent technologies, not just internally coined phrases. A query-fragile search produces false negatives.
ce_014_false_negative_search_lesson.what_happened: The Round 56q 12-search prior-art attack MISSED US11304793B2 because the search used internally coined terminology ('adaptive venous stent', 'sensing stent', 'flow regulating venous implant') rather than the patent's actual language ('cerebrospinal venous insufficiency', 'tunable endovascular device', 'deformable constraining member').
what_to_avoid: Do not conclude 'no prior art found' based on keyword searches using internally coined terminology
Do not assume absence of results for our formulation means the capability is novel
Future patent searches must include CPC class traversal, inventor/assignee neighbor search, adjacent technology terminology, and backward/forward citation chains

narrow_gap_search.question: What can adaptive transverse/sigmoid sinus regulation do that US11304793B2's IJV architecture CANNOT?
patents_found: US20220031488A1: intracranial venous sinus stent with variable cell size (STATIC, not adaptive)
US20200406018A1: drug delivery to IPS (not adaptive stent)

key_anatomical_difference.ijv: Extracranial, venous wall, carries blood FROM brain. No arachnoid granulations.
key_anatomical_difference.transverse_sigmoid_sinuses: Intracranial, DURAL wall, site of arachnoid granulations (CSF absorption). Directly affects CSF dynamics.

key_physiological_effect_difference.transverse_sigmoid_adaptive_stent: Could regulate CSF ABSORPTION at arachnoid granulation site (CSF dynamic) — a different physiological effect

narrow_gap_search.frontier_evidence: Nature 2026 (El Kamouh): 'brain sinuses are dynamic vascular gateways that actively regulate pressure inside the skull' — supports the concept that sinus-level regulation has unique physiological effects.
narrow_gap_search.section_102: NOT anticipated for transverse/sigmoid + IIH + CSF absorption regulation
narrow_gap_search.section_103: SERIOUS THREAT — obvious anatomical transfer from IJV to transverse sinus
narrow_gap_search.surviving_question: Can adaptive transverse/sigmoid sinus stent regulate CSF ABSORPTION (not just venous return) — an effect US11304793B2 CANNOT produce because IJV has no arachnoid granulations?

verdict.res4_narrow_gap: NOT YET ESTABLISHED — biologically plausible but legally fragile
verdict.ce_014_lesson: Query-fragile searches produce false negatives; use patent vocabulary not our vocabulary
verdict.narrow_gap_section_103: SERIOUS THREAT (obvious anatomical transfer from IJV to sinus)
